MARKETPLACE GROWTH & SELLER INTELLIGENCE

Marketplace scale is substantial.
The management challenge is growth quality.

MarketLens is a historical marketplace decision-support analysis built on Olist’s Brazilian E-Commerce and Marketing Funnel datasets. It connects seller acquisition, activation, retention, commercial concentration, and customer experience to a governed set of management actions.

Historical anonymized case study · Olist Brazil · Executive complete-period reporting through Aug 2018 · Observational evidence

01 · EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

What leaders need to know

The analysis surfaces five management messages. Two concern measurement and governance; three concern marketplace operating risk. The evidence is intentionally conservative: association is never presented as causality.

01
Measurement trust

The apparent end-of-period collapse is a reporting-boundary issue, not a confirmed commercial collapse.

Raw order observations extend to 12 Nov 2018, but the final decision-eligible complete month is 31 Aug 2018. September contains only 16 orders and October only 4, so those edge periods must be excluded or visibly flagged before executive trend interpretation.

Management implicationEvery executive refresh should carry a completeness gate before trend claims are published.
2018-08-31last executive-complete period
02
Acquisition quality

Lead origin matters for observed conversion, but conversion alone is not enough to govern acquisition.

Across 8,000 MQLs, origin is associated with conversion. Paid Search converts at 12.3%, Organic Search at 11.8%, and Social at 5.6%. M3 retention contrasts remain imprecise after adjustment, so retention is a guardrail rather than a channel-ranking KPI.

Management implicationUse volume, conversion, downstream matched-seller value, activation, and retention together.
0.131Cramér’s V
03
Activation

Seller time-to-value is slow after conversion.

Only 15.8% of observable closed sellers activate within 30 days, 30.8% within 60 days, and 42.1% within 90 days. Among observed activators, median time to first sale is 44.3 days.

Management implicationInstrument onboarding at 7/30/60-day checkpoints and test interventions against retention and downstream seller value.
15.8%30-day activation
04
Commercial resilience

Marketplace value is highly concentrated in a small seller cohort.

Seller GMV has a Gini coefficient of 0.792. The top 1% / 5% / 10% / 20% of positive-GMV sellers account for approximately 26.1% / 53.3% / 67.6% / 82.7% of seller GMV proxy.

Management implicationTreat concentration as a monitoring signal and pair it with category breadth and service quality before intervention.
82.7%GMV from top 20%
05
Customer experience

Late delivery is strongly associated with weaker review outcomes.

Late orders average 2.57 review points versus 4.29 for on-time orders. Their low-review rate is 54.0% versus 9.2%, a +44.8 percentage-point difference and 5.87× observed risk ratio.

Management implicationPrioritize delivery investigation by volume × delay severity × review penalty, then test changes before broad rollout.
5.87×observed low-review risk ratio

08 · ROOT CAUSE

Six cases, twenty hypotheses — with supported, rejected, and inconclusive paths separated

Root-cause work is treated as hypothesis management rather than storytelling. Each case records evidence for, evidence against, alternative explanations, a status, and a decision boundary.

ConfirmedRC1 · Reporting boundary

Incomplete edge periods can mimic a business collapse.

Gate executive reporting on period completeness before escalating a commercial problem.

AssociationRC2 · Acquisition quality

Origin is associated with conversion; volume-only optimization is rejected.

Retention evidence is not strong enough to crown an origin winner.

Supported signalRC3 · Activation bottleneck

Seller onboarding has a long time-to-value.

Instrument the journey rather than assuming origin itself explains activation speed.

Risk signalRC4 · Concentration

Seller value is concentrated; generic diversification is not yet justified.

Target category breadth where value and dependency intersect.

AssociationRC5 · Delivery & reviews

Lateness is associated with weaker reviews; single-seller blame is rejected.

Investigate category, state, route, carrier, and delay severity.

Diagnostic pathRC6 · Category underperformance

Cool Stuff fell 46.5% from Jul to Aug 2018, but the mechanism is not yet identified.

Split orders vs AOV, then seller breadth/productivity, with CX as a guardrail.

11 · METHODOLOGY & GOVERNANCE

The analytical contract behind the report

Business conclusions are separated from measurement rules, eligibility rules, statistical evidence, and limitations.

01

Grain-safe modeling

GMV is calculated from item grain before one-to-many payment joins. Delivery and review analysis stays at order grain.

02

Decision-eligible periods

Incomplete edge months are flagged before trend claims. Executive complete reporting ends 31 Aug 2018.

03

Eligibility-aware activation

30/60/90-day rates use sellers observable for the full window. Censored sellers remain visible instead of being mislabeled as failures.

04

Retention observability

M3 retention excludes cohorts too young to observe. Origin effects remain a guardrail when uncertainty is wide.

05

Statistical discipline

Effect sizes, confidence intervals, FDR-adjusted pairwise comparisons, bootstrap evidence, and an adjusted GLM accompany descriptive results.

06

Claim governance

Claims are classified by evidence strength. Observational findings are explicitly separated from causal conclusions.

INTERPRETATION BOUNDARY

Historical anonymized case study, not a current-market forecast.

GMV is a proxy rather than platform revenue or profit. Marketing cost is unavailable, so CAC and ROAS are not estimated. Operational and channel findings are observational; they may reflect selection, mix, timing, or unmeasured confounding. Current business action would require refreshed production data and controlled follow-up tests.

MARKETLENS · FINAL EXECUTIVE CASE STUDY

From trustworthy measurement to an operating decision agenda.

The project demonstrates end-to-end analytical work: data modeling, metric governance, statistical diagnostics, Power BI reporting, root-cause reasoning, and decision design.
